us_cwa_316b.label: US cooling-water intake rules
us_cwa_316b.source: Clean Water Act §316(b) and 40 CFR Part 125 (2 MGD design-intake trigger, 25 % cooling-use test, and the 1 % tidal-excursion-volume test for new facilities in estuaries at 40 CFR 125.84)

ca_fisheries_act.label: Fisheries Act (Canada)
ca_fisheries_act.source: Fisheries Act s.34(1), s.35 and s.36(3): water changed by heat can be a deleterious substance, and intake works can harmfully alter fish habitat. No numeric intake threshold.

none.label: No intake rule applied
none.source: This repository does not yet transcribe an intake rule for this jurisdiction. The §316(b) arithmetic is still shown for comparison but no intake requirement is asserted.

jurisdictions.label: Washington (United States)
jurisdictions.note: Marine water-body categories set a 1-DMax criterion; a point source may add no more than 12/(T-2) °C at the edge of the mixing zone, and no more than 0.3 °C where the criterion is already exceeded naturally. Pick the category for the receiving water below.

jurisdictions.label: California (United States)
jurisdictions.temperature_source: California Thermal Plan §3.B.(3)–(4), coastal waters, new discharges (SWRCB; text transcribed in data/checks/ca_thermal_plan.md)
jurisdictions.note: New coastal discharges: no more than 4 °F (2.22 °C) above natural at the shoreline, the ocean substrate, or the ocean surface beyond 1,000 ft, and no more than 20 °F (11.1 °C) above natural at the discharge itself.

jurisdictions.label: Oregon (United States)
jurisdictions.note: Oregon's numeric temperature standard is not transcribed in this repository, so no state increment is applied. Enter the increment from the applicable standard or permit. Federal intake rules still apply.
jurisdictions.verify_note: Needs Oregon's temperature standard transcribed from the primary rule text before this jurisdiction can carry a numeric increment.

jurisdictions.label: Other United States state or federal waters
jurisdictions.note: Federal intake rules apply nationally, but this repository transcribes state temperature standards only for Washington and California. Enter the increment your state standard or permit sets.
jurisdictions.verify_note: No state temperature standard transcribed; the increment is user-supplied.

jurisdictions.label: British Columbia (Canada)
jurisdictions.note: British Columbia sets thermal limits in the waste discharge authorisation issued under the Environmental Management Act, so the numeric increment is permit-specific rather than a published standard. Enter the increment the authorisation sets.
jurisdictions.verify_note: Permit-specific: no published numeric marine thermal increment is transcribed in this repository.

jurisdictions.label: European Union member state
jurisdictions.note: Water temperature is a supporting element of ecological status under the Water Framework Directive, but the numeric limit comes from the member state's water permit. Enter that increment. EU law sets no cooling-water intake screening rule equivalent to §316(b).
jurisdictions.verify_note: Member-state permit values and any national thermal standard are not transcribed in this repository.

jurisdictions.label: Other or not listed
jurisdictions.note: No jurisdiction-specific rule is applied and no intake requirement is asserted. Enter the increment from the applicable standard or permit and treat the result as arithmetic only.
jurisdictions.verify_note: No rules transcribed for this selection.
